title: CRO Manager - E-Commerce (m/w/d) in Vollzeit
description:
🚀 Globalist ist DIE führende Performance-Marketing-Agentur für nationale und internationale digitale Marketingstrategien, made in Stuttgart!

Unsere Agentur ist in Paid Search, Paid Social und Organic Search unterteilt und betreut bereits über 370 Kunden. Wir verwalten jährlich 60 Mio. € Werbebudget und kombinieren Strategie mit operativer Skalierungsexpertise. Dank direkter Google- und Meta-Schulungen setzen wir auf moderne, datengetriebene Performance-Optimierung.

Zu unseren Kunden gehören Boehringer Ingelheim, La Marzocco, Nø Cosmetics, ASAM BEAUTY und viele mehr!

Was uns unterscheidet: Unser Herz schlägt für den eCommerce. Wir betreuen nicht nur Top-Brands, sondern betreiben auch eigene eCommerce-Shops. Das bedeutet, du kannst dich über das reine Design hinaus in Bereichen wie Nutzerforschung, datengetriebene Optimierung und Shopify-Ökosysteme weiterentwickeln und die Ergebnisse deiner Arbeit direkt an echten Umsatzzahlen messen.

Aufgaben

Als CRO Manager bei Globalist optimierst du E-Commerce-Shops so, dass aus Besuchern Käufer werden – datenbasiert, hypothesengetrieben und mit direktem Impact auf den Umsatz unserer Kunden. Du bist die Schnittstelle zwischen Daten, Design und Entwicklung und steuerst CRO-Projekte von der Analyse bis zur Umsetzung.

Das erwartet dich konkret bei uns:

  • Du analysierst Conversion Funnels, Nutzerverhalten und Shop-Performance unserer E-Commerce-Kunden mit GA4, Heatmap-Tools und Session Recordings – und leitest daraus konkrete Optimierungshypothesen ab.
  • Du konzipierst A/B-Tests und Personalisierungsmaßnahmen, priorisierst sie nach Uplift-Potenzial und begleitest den gesamten Testing-Prozess bis zur statistisch validen Auswertung.
  • Du übernimmst das Stakeholder Management gegenüber unseren Kunden: Du präsentierst Testergebnisse, erklärst komplexe CRO-Zusammenhänge verständlich und leitest klare Handlungsempfehlungen ab.
  • Du erstellst Wireframes und klickbare Prototypen in Figma, um Optimierungsideen schnell greifbar zu machen – für Kunden, Entwickler und interne Teams.
  • Du arbeitest eng mit Webentwicklern zusammen und bringst grundlegendes technisches Verständnis (HTML/CSS, JavaScript-Basics) mit, um Umsetzungen zu begleiten und zu prüfen.
  • Du arbeitest crossfunktional mit unseren SEA-, Paid-Social- und SEO-Teams, um kanalübergreifende Optimierungspotenziale zu identifizieren und gemeinsam zu heben.

Qualifikation

Das bringst du mit (Muss):

  • 2–3 Jahre Berufserfahrung im Bereich CRO, E-Commerce oder UX – idealerweise in einer Agentur oder einem E-Commerce-Unternehmen
  • Nachweisbare Erfahrung im E-Commerce: Du kennst typische Funnel-Strukturen, weißt, wo Shops verlieren und was Conversion-Hebel im Online-Handel sind
  • Sicheres Stakeholder Management: Du kannst Testergebnisse und Optimierungsstrategien gegenüber Kunden klar kommunizieren und überzeugend vertreten
  • Sicherer Umgang mit Figma – du kannst Hypothesen in Wireframes und Prototypen übersetzen, ohne auf Entwickler warten zu müssen
  • Grundlegendes technisches Verständnis (HTML/CSS, JavaScript-Basics), um mit Entwicklern auf Augenhöhe zu kommunizieren und Implementierungen zu prüfen
  • Erfahrung mit A/B-Testing-Tools (z.B. VWO, Optimizely, AB Tasty) und Google Analytics / GA4
  • Fließende Deutschkenntnisse (C1) für die direkte Kundenberatung

Das wäre das Sahnehäubchen (Kann):

  • Erfahrung mit Heatmap- und Session-Recording-Tools wie Hotjar oder Microsoft Clarity
  • Kenntnisse in Shopify, Shopware oder anderen E-Commerce-Systemen
  • Interesse an AI-gestützter Optimierung und GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)

Benefits

Bei Globalist arbeitest du in einem crossfunktionalen Team, das Performance nicht nur für Kunden denkt, sondern auch für sich selbst lebt. CRO ist bei uns kein Silo – du arbeitest täglich mit SEA-, SEO- und Paid-Social-Experten zusammen und profitierst von einem breiten Wissenspool. Learnings werden offen geteilt, Testergebnisse gemeinsam gefeiert. Unsere eigenen E-Com-Brands im Fashion- und Outdoor-Bereich dienen dir als Playground: Neue Hypothesen testen, bevor sie auf Kundenprojekte skaliert werden.

Dein Arbeitsalltag:

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten 🕗
  • Modernes Office direkt in der Stuttgarter Innenstadt mit Dachterrasse ☀️
  • Höhenverstellbare Tische und eigenes MacBook bei Festanstellung 💻

Deine Entwicklung:

  • Regelmäßige Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten und langfristige Karriereperspektive 🎓
  • Einblicke über CRO hinaus – Supply Chain, Product Development, Shop-Systeme und Paid Marketing
  • Regelmäßige Feedbackgespräche, damit du dein volles Potenzial ausschöpfen kannst

Deine Extras:

  • Kostenloses DB-Deutschlandticket oder Parkplatz in der Innenstadt 🚗
  • E-Gym Wellpass für deine Fitness und Gesundheit 🏋🏽
  • Kostenlose Getränke und Kaffee im Office 🥤
  • Regelmäßige Firmenveranstaltungen und Teamevents 🍾

Für uns selbstverständlich:

  • Großartiger Team-Spirit und wertschätzende Atmosphäre 😊
  • Flache Hierarchien und kurze Entscheidungswege
  • Strukturiertes Onboarding ab Tag 1 👋

Klingt nach dir? Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung – gerne mit konkreten Beispielen oder Cases, die zeigen, wie du Conversion Rates im E-Commerce messbar verbessert hast.

Senior Product Manager (f/m/d)
description:
About us

Zenjob is an AI-powered flexible staffing platform that has connected companies and temporary workers since 2015. Companies use our platform to book ready-to-work staff in real time, while students use our app - we call them Zenjobbers - to find part-time jobs that conveniently fit around their studies. Over 40,000 Zenjobbers and 1,000 partner companies from logistics, retail, and hospitality in all major German cities share our belief that good work is not a coincidence. It is the result of innovative technology and genuine commitment. Good work starts here.

The Role

We are seeking a highly skilled Senior Product Manager to join our team. In this role, you will play a key part in defining and executing a product vision that ensures Zenjob’s marketplace dynamics are well balanced, by optimizing our demand forecast, making sure jobs and Zenjobbers are matched optimally, and engaging students in working a high number of shifts.

This is not a role that owns one squad's backlog. You'll work project-based: form a team around a problem, own it end-to-end until it delivers on the expected need. You'll get problem statements, not requirements documents. Recent examples: how shifts get allocated across thousands of Zenjobbers each week, and how we get a new Zenjobber from signup to their first shift without human intervention.

This role suits a Product Manager who is energised by an open-ended problem, and who finds complex workflows genuinely interesting. You'll report to the Director of Product and work across our Supply, Demand and Staffing squads, depending on the problem to solve.

What You’ll do

  • Bring our business goals to reality. Understand our financial goals, our users' problems and transform them into solutions that drive our revenue up.

  • Talk to users directly. Zenjobbers, clients, and our own internal teams. Most of the good opportunities come out of these conversations, not out of a backlog.

  • Do your own data work. You don’t wait until a data analyst gives you the insights, you dive into it and derive them yourself.

  • Turn ambiguity into a defensible plan. Take a problem nobody agrees on yet, and define what we're solving, what we're explicitly not solving, and in what order.

  • Design and run tests. Form a hypothesis, define what would falsify it, ship the smallest thing that gives you a real answer, and be honest about the result.

  • Drive product development from concept to launch. Pull together Engineering, Design, Ops and Commercial around a problem and keep them moving through hypothesis, building, rollout and post-launch decision making

  • Own the outcome, not the output. Each project has a number attached. You define what success looks like up front, and you're the one who says whether it was hit.

  • Communicate clearly. A one-page memo an exec can act on. A spec an engineer doesn't have to interpret. A tradeoff explained to Commercial in terms they care about.

What we’re looking for

  • 6+ years in product, with meaningful time on products where the software coordinates real-world processes - staffing, logistics, fintech ops, healthcare, or similar, with substantial business impact. You have experience in marketplace dynamics and allocation problems.

  • You've shipped something complex end-to-end and can talk credibly about what broke, not just what launched.

  • You're analytically strong - comfortable getting to an answer yourself rather than commissioning one, and having a fluent conversation with data scientists.

  • You've moved teams you don't manage. Cross-functional influence without formal authority is most of this job.

  • You write and speak clearly. This is the strongest single signal we look for, because in a cross-team role, clear communication is most of how work actually moves.

  • AI is already part of how you work, and you can say specifically where it helps and where it doesn't, and you are already able to ship small features with little to no help from Engineers

  • English fluency. German is a big plus.

What we offer

  • Real ownership of problems that visibly move the business - not a slice of someone else's roadmap.

  • Innovative mission: Together we create something new. Work in a dynamic set-up where you learn a lot and your every idea is heard.

  • Unique team spirit: We can rely on each other blindly and celebrate all successes together as a team.

  • Vacation: Recreation and further education is important, which is why we offer 28 days of paid vacation (increased by 1 day for every 2 calendar years of service with us, up to a maximum of 30 days), 1 day of special leave for community service, 5 days of paid educational leave, and the possibility of unpaid leave

  • Hybrid working model: We love our brand new office in Prenzlauer Berg. But sometimes you need a little more flexibility. Zenjob’s flexible working model combines the best of both worlds, so you can work remotely up to 2 days / week (1 day, during the first 6 months, so we can guarantee you the best onboarding).

  • Dog-lover: If you have a dog, feel free to bring it with you. We don’t bite and always have a bowl of water in our range of drinks

  • Personal growth: Ongoing focus on your personal development (annual training budget of EUR 750, mentoring opportunities, constant career development conversations)

  • Healthy mind in a healthy body: With us you will receive a 30 EUR Urban Sports Club grant to keep you fit. In addition, we have a small sports room in the office ourselves.

  • Always mobile: You will receive EUR 40 credit per month for NAVIT, a sustainable mobility tool for public transport, bike sharing and much more.

  • Legendary Events: Quarterly team events, winter and summer parties, budget for birthdays and anniversaries of our employees

If this sounds good, then we’d love to find out more about you! Apply and send in your application.

🎥 Watch our Office Tour video.

We invite you to visit our careers page, follow our LinkedIn page and connect with us on Instagram.

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to judging every qualified individual on their ability, regardless of age, gender identity, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability status, or religion. There is no need to add your photo and age to the application.

title: Senior Data Platform Engineer
description:
We are looking for a Senior Data Platform Engineer to join the Data Platform at Smartly!

Smartly is building the standard path for governed data sharing across product services, analytics, and AI/ML. The Data Platform team owns the contracts, control mechanisms, publication paths, catalog metadata, lifecycle rules, lineage, permissions, and runtime building blocks that make reusable data safe and practical at scale.

This is a role for someone who wants to shape a platform early, while working on concrete production problems from the start. Smartly already has the production systems, Kafka backbone, PostgreSQL databases, analytical consumers, and AI/ML use cases that need a better data foundation. The challenge is to turn that reality into a standard path that engineers actually want to use.

Our first milestone is focused: centrally managed publishing tables in service-owned PostgreSQL databases, captured through Debezium CDC into Kafka, and registered in DataHub with ownership, lifecycle, lineage, and impact-analysis metadata. Longer-term, the platform expands toward self-service data products, governed materialisations, durable shared state, and reusable data across Smartly's operational and analytical systems.

This is not a role where you only maintain an existing reporting pipeline. You will help design and build the platform path that other engineering teams use when they publish and consume shared data.

What you will do

  • Design and build platform services, tools, and workflows for contract-driven data publishing and consumption.
  • Build the first production path for platform-managed PostgreSQL publishing tables, Debezium CDC, Kafka topics, and catalog registration.
  • Create GitOps-style workflows where contracts, schemas, ownership, lifecycle, compatibility, policy metadata, and runtime desired state are reviewed, validated, and reconciled as code.
  • Build tooling that gives product engineers fast feedback before they publish or change data products.
  • Help define how Smartly models data products, publishing contracts, schema evolution, field stability, deletion semantics, access policy, lineage, and cost attribution.
  • Operate and improve the CDC runtime model, including Kubernetes workloads, source-specific isolation, offsets, schema history, heartbeats, signal channels, lag visibility, replay, resnapshotting, and recovery.
  • Integrate platform metadata into DataHub so engineers can discover data products, understand ownership, trace lineage, and reason about the impact of changes.
  • Work with product, infrastructure, data engineering, analytics, and AI/ML teams to make the standard path easier and safer than bespoke point-to-point integrations.

What we are looking for

  • Strong experience building and operating production software systems, preferably in platform, infrastructure, backend, or data-intensive environments.
  • Deep understanding of distributed systems trade-offs: reliability, idempotency, replay, eventual consistency, ownership boundaries, compatibility, and operational failure modes.
  • Practical experience with PostgreSQL or other relational databases, including schema design, migrations, transactions, replication, or operational performance.
  • Experience with Kafka, event streaming, CDC, Debezium, or adjacent data-movement technologies. Direct Debezium experience is valuable, but strong fundamentals matter more.
  • Experience building software that other engineers use: CLIs, internal platforms, control planes, automation, CI validation, developer tooling, or self-service workflows.
  • Familiarity with Kubernetes and cloud or infrastructure platforms, including runtime isolation, deployment, observability, and operational ownership.
  • Ability to turn ambiguous architectural direction into practical increments, make trade-offs explicit, and deliver useful production systems without waiting for perfect certainty.
  • Clear written and spoken communication in English. This role involves aligning multiple engineering teams around standards, contracts, and ownership boundaries.

Useful experience, but not required

  • DataHub or other data catalog, lineage, or governance systems.
  • Open table formats such as Apache Iceberg, object-store-backed data lakes, S3, BigQuery, ClickHouse, or analytical storage systems.
  • GitHub Actions, policy-as-code, infrastructure-as-code, controllers, operators, or reconciliation-based systems.
  • Data contracts, schema registries, Protobuf, Avro, JSON Schema, compatibility checking, field-level metadata, or contract testing.
  • Experience supporting analytics, AI/ML, feature-store-style access patterns, or cross-domain product-service integrations.
  • Experience with JVM languages and Python, TypeScript, Go, or Ruby.

What we offer you

At Smartly, we offer a place where you can do meaningful technical work while growing with a global team.

  • Inclusive global culture built on trust, transparency, open feedback, and respect for different perspectives.
  • Global impact through technology used by major brands to plan, create, optimize, and understand digital advertising at scale.
  • Wellbeing support, paid holidays, family leave, and sustainable ways of working.
  • Equity options, performance-based rewards, competitive compensation, and career development opportunities.
  • A flexible hybrid workplace that balances office collaboration with focused remote work. At Smartly we work 3 days a week from the office.

About Smartly

Smartly is an advertising technology company helping brands create, manage, optimize, and understand digital advertising across major media platforms. Our engineering organization builds the systems that connect media, creative, and intelligence capabilities into a product used by customers globally.

We value clear communication, ownership, curiosity, and collaboration across teams. We want Smartly to be a place where people can do strong work, grow, and feel respected.

Not sure you tick every box? Please apply anyway. We care about strong engineering fundamentals, ownership, curiosity, and the ability to build reliable systems with others. Direct experience with every technology listed here is less important than the judgment to learn, reason from first principles, and ship useful platform capabilities.

About Smartly

Smartly is the AI-powered advertising technology company transforming ad experiences for brands and their consumers. Our comprehensive advertising platform seamlessly integrates the capabilities of media, creative, and intelligence to power more than 800 billion impressions and generate more than 300 billion creatives annually, delivering tangible business outcomes for brands and advertisers.

Smartly is the only company in the industry recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave: Creative Advertising Technologies with PwC validating the results it delivers for brands. We manage creative and media for 700+ brands worldwide and $6B in ad spend across the largest media platforms, including Facebook, Google, Instagram, Pinterest, Snap, and TikTok. Our end-to-end technology, unmatched access to media platforms and exceptional customer service help Fortune 500 brands to reach and engage consumers and learn what performs best.Smartly is a multinational and diverse team of 750+ Smartlies from 60+ nationalities, working in 13 countries. Together, we want to create and maintain an inclusive environment where everyone feels respected and heard. Our Diversity, Equity & Inclusion approach is at the heart of it.

Visit Smartly to learn more.

title: Delivery Manager - Heating and cooling (m/f/d)
description:
1KOMMA5°

At 1KOMMA5°, we pursue a clear vision: Living on wind and sunlight forever for free. To make this a reality, we are building the energy system of the future with Heartbeat AI. Want to be part of it?

You will focus on coordinating our Integrations Team, managing our partner network, drafting requirements for their software and hardware solutions, and engaging in root cause analyses to provide a high platform stability. You will ensure the best is yet to come when it comes to heat pumps

Key responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Coordination: Have an overarching view of all heat pump optimization topics and how they fit into the overall Heartbeat technology stack. Track and report all workstreams upwards and downwards and ensure alignment with workstreams from other teams.

  • Act as a point of contact for our heat pump OEM partners, supporting efforts to adapt and integrate their solutions with our systems and ensure that things are always running smoothly for our customers.

Dein Profil

  • Proven experience in managing complex technical projects that span the intersection of hardware and software products
  • Broad knowledge of various communication protocols typical for the renewable energy and HVAC markets like Modbus, EEBUS, etc.

  • Passion for maintaining a well-documented knowledge base to share information across the organisation and engage with senior leaders
  • Experience or highly passionate about building innovative energy market solutions that challenge the status quo and usher in a new era of affordable and renewable energy for everyone
  • Fun in solving technical challenges together with internal and external partners while owning the project execution and communicating in an effective manner
  • An agile and product-oriented mindset and you consider yourself a team player
  • Very strong written and spoken English and German skills

Bonus points for:

  • Experience with EEBUS and Modbus TCP hardware integration

Benefits

title: Senior Go Developer (f/m/d) – Focus on gRPC & Enterprise Applications
description:
You'd build the Natuvion Cloud Portal, the Go/gRPC platform at the center of the company. It's the cloud counterpart to our core products and the central access point nearly every team works through, used by our own people and our customers alike. A year old, already the strategic core, mostly greenfield, and growing fast.

What to expect

The work is varied, and the problems rarely repeat. One stretch you might be making multi-tenant queries fly across 100 GiB+ tables in DuckDB; the next, packing a couple dozen services into a single binary a customer can run on-prem, or building our AI firewall, deep-packet inspection for AI traffic that decides, per customer and per user, exactly which AI tools and MCP servers are allowed. It's the kind of fine-grained control that enterprises with sensitive data actually need and almost nobody has built.

The stack is deliberately solid, though we'll reach for newer tools where the benefit is substantial. Go and gRPC throughout, with Google's AIPs as a strict ruleset so our APIs stay compatible as the platform grows. We run on AWS/EKS and on-prem with no vendor lock-in, backed by PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, Redis, OpenSearch and a Grafana/Loki/Mimir/Jaeger stack, all shipped through GitHub Actions. Authorization is one such case: the platform's entire authz system is built on SpiceDB/Zanzibar, newer and less battle-tested, but exactly the right tool for the job. There's a dedicated SRE team, but you build it, you run it. You'd join four backend engineers, a flat team with a hands-on technical lead, and we're hiring across backend and frontend to keep up.

Your Responsibilities :

  • Design and build the gRPC services at the heart of the Cloud Portal, APIs that other teams depend on and that must stay compatible as the platform grows

  • Take services end to end: design, ship, and run them in production, across both cloud and on-prem

  • Solve the performance and scaling problems that come with multi-tenant systems and large datasets

  • Help shape architecture and technical direction, where your input genuinely moves things in a team this small


  • 5+ years writing production-grade Go

  • Strong grasp of idiomatic Go, concurrency patterns, and profiling with pprof, plus a real understanding of escape analysis, allocation behavior, and what the GC is actually doing

  • Solid experience building and maintaining APIs using gRPC, including Protobuf versioning, streaming, and API lifecycle best practices (bonus: you know Google AIPs)

  • Proven experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL), performance tuning, and schema design

  • Comfortable in cloud-native environments, applying caching, queuing, and observability best practices

  • Professional working proficiency in English, enough to communicate complex technical ideas clearly to peers and stakeholders

If you think that you don't meet all the requirements: With us, there are "no limits" to your development! Go your way with us - we support you! Just show us who you are.

What you can expect from us:

An environment that is always open to change and optimization. There is no "it's always been like this" with us. You have the opportunity to contribute your knowledge, design processes, standardize existing topics or optimize workflows. Be a source of inspiration and bring us even further forward with your expertise!

We create conditions in which you feel comfortable:

  • Home office contracts & absolute flexibility through free organization of working hours

  • Permanent position and 30 days of vacation

  • FlexWork: Work remotely from other European countries for up to 3 months per year

  • Monthly budget for individually selectable benefits from over 50 possible offers via emplu, various offers via corporate benefits, as well as bicycle and car leasing via salary conversion

  • Mental Health Benefit 'Nilo' – 10 free sessions with psychologists annually as well as access to meditations and courses

  • We provide you with targeted support in your professional and personal development at Natuvion

  • Mentoring program for a structured and personal induction

  • Be part of the #teamgreen - At Natuvion, you'll work on innovative projects as part of a team that stands up for each other. We rely on cooperation, openness and trust

  • Modern equipment and central offices in Walldorf, Berlin, Munich and Leipzig

  • Your long-term perspective is important to us, which is why we subsidize your company pension scheme as well as capital-forming benefits

Join #teamgreen - Natuvion is a digital moving company.

Our team does not move tables, filing cabinets or chairs. Natuvion transports business-critical data and processes from one technology platform to another. Typical Natuvion "relocation services" include data migration, data transformation, data integration, data privacy, data security, and data quality.

Our >400 consultants and developers in Germany, Austria, Slovakia, the USA and Australia have extensive know-how in (SAP)® projects and a profound understanding of processes across industry boundaries. With a lot of experience, commitment and commitment, they support our customers with advice, services and their own software technology. In this way, we enable companies to always use their data and processes on the most modern and innovative platforms.

Are you interested? We look forward to receiving your application and getting to know you!
Feel free to send us your CV, we do not need a cover letter.

title: (Senior) Full Stack Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
We are a small engineering team inside Natuvion that finds and builds the next high-value additions to Natuvion's

product portfolio. We build DCS Compose, a modern language for enterprise data transformations with deep integration

into the Natuvion Cloud.

Our work has three main aspects

  • Understanding the domain. We make Natuvion's transformation knowledge searchable, structured, and available to AI agents. Hundreds of customer projects have produced millions of lines of transformation content. We build the infrastructure that turns this accumulated knowledge into a usable asset.

  • User focused development. We understand our users and develop tools and applications for them. Our mission is to help our users excel at their work by providing them with the technical means to do so.

  • Technical ownership. We develop solutions with deep integration into Natuvion's cloud landscape. We develop the backend and frontend functionality keeping in mind performance, adaptability and correctness.

We build on top of the Natuvion Cloud, using its APIs and shared components as our foundation.

The cloud team scales the platform; we focus on what to build on it.

The team has strong technical and scientific backgrounds. We care about quality even in prototypes: Disciplined engineering, not vibe-coding.

We're part of Natuvion (~500 employees, SAP Gold Partner). That means access to enterprise customers, real

transformation projects, and corporate backing, with the autonomy of a small team.

Why Join Us

  • Real problems, not toy projects. Enterprise data transformations involve millions of records, complex business rules, and tight timelines. The prototypes you build here solve real problems for real customers.

  • End-to-end ownership. From observing a process in a customer project to shipping a working prototype. You decide what to build and how.

  • AI as a daily tool, not a buzzword. We use agentic coding and AI-assisted development and help the organization

    with AI usage.

  • Small team, big reach. A few people with direct access to enterprise customers like BMW, Volkswagen, E.ON and Lufthansa, a cloud platform to build on, and the freedom to move fast.

Your Responsibilities

  • Build features for the DCS Compose application on top of the Natuvion Cloud: frontend, backend, and API integrations.

  • Develop UI components for the content corpus: search interfaces, data visualization, and comparison tools.

  • Integrate AI capabilities into applications: MCP, semantic search, and embeddings.

  • Use and extend NCP's shared frontend components and APIs as building blocks for new solutions.

  • Maintain quality standards: testing, code review, and clean architecture — even when moving fast.


Your Profile

  • Strong frontend and backend skills. You're comfortable building both sides of a web application.

  • Experience with API design and consuming platform APIs.

  • Familiarity with modern TypeScript, React (preferrably NextJS) and Golang.

  • Knowledge in Protobuf and gRPC is a plus.

  • An eye for good UI. You build interfaces people actually want to use.

  • Quality discipline. You write tests, you review code, and you care about maintainability.

How We Work

  • Prototyping with standards. We ship fast, but not at all costs. Prototypes have tests, clean APIs, and documentation.

    When a prototype proves its value, it should be ready to hand off and not rewritten from scratch.

  • Our current stack: Golang, gRPC, TypeScript, NextJS. We build on Natuvion Cloud's APIs and shared frontend components.

  • The stack evolves as the problems do. We pick the right tool, not the familiar one.

  • Agentic coding as a discipline. We use AI-assisted development tools daily. We hold the same quality standards whether code was written by a human or an agent.

What you can expect from us

An environment that is always open to change and optimization. There is no "it's always been like this" with us. You have the opportunity to contribute your knowledge, design processes, standardize existing topics or optimize workflows. Be a source of inspiration and bring us even further forward with your expertise!

We create conditions in which you feel comfortable

  • Home office contracts & absolute flexibility through free organization of working hours

  • Permanent position and 30 days of vacation

  • FlexWork: Work remotely from other European countries for up to 3 months per year

  • Monthly budget for individually selectable benefits from over 50 possible offers via emplu, various offers via corporate benefits, as well as bicycle and car leasing via salary conversion

Natuvion builds software and provides consulting for enterprise data transformations — migrations, restructurings,

title: Working Student IT Operations (m/f/d)
description:
Hi!

We are Coffee Circle, Germany’s leading sustainable specialty coffee roastery based in Berlin. We offer the world’s finest coffee and equipment to over 150,000 customers online and in our Cafés, driven by our goal to make high-end coffee experiences enjoyable and accessible to all. We foster direct trade relationships with coffee farmers worldwide, pay high prices for the coffee beans, and ensure everyone involved in the value chain gets treated fairly and respectfully. For every kilogram of coffee we sell, we invest € 1 through our Coffee Circle Foundation e.V. to help support sustainable improvements in coffee-growing areas, such as providing clean drinking water, hygiene training, and coffee labs. With over 5 million euros raised in donations, we cannot wait to increase our positive impact with you on our team, one cup of coffee at a time.

Your role

  • Support the IT setup across our cafés, office, and warehouse, from POS systems and printers to tablets, routers, and Raspberry Pis.
  • Keep our UniFi networks and internet connections running and help troubleshoot issues remotely or on-site.
  • Maintain and provision devices, keep our hardware inventory clean, and support onboarding and offboarding.
  • Document setups, fixes, and processes in Notion so knowledge stays accessible.
  • Support practical GDPR and information security topics, including TOMs, deletion concepts, access management, and security documentation.
  • Report to our CTO and be part of our Tech Team.

Your profile
  • You’re currently enrolled at university, ideally in Computer Science, Business Informatics, or a related field.
  • You have a basic understanding of networks and Linux and enjoy learning new technical topics.
  • You work independently, stay organized, and appreciate good documentation.
  • You have experience with UniFi, GDPR or ISO 27001 is a plus, not a must.
  • You’re happy to travel between our Berlin locations when needed. Being based in Berlin and working mainly onsite is non-negotiable for this role.
  • You are available 20 hours a week, 3 days a week. Based on your availability, you can choose the days you work (Monday to Saturday).
  • You’re fluent in English; German is a plus.

title: Senior Brand Partnerships & Licensing Manager (All Genders)
description:
YOU & AHEAD

At ahead, we are on a mission to clean up the world's candy drawers. We make the snacks everyone actually craves, reformulated with less sugar and zero compromise on taste. We are 120 people strong, with 170+ SKUs and aggressive growth across D2C, retail, Amazon, and new European markets.

Our Brand Activation department is where we move from product to culture. We do that through limited editions: co-branded drops with entertainment IPs, licensing deals with cultural icons, collaborations that make people genuinely excited about what they are eating.

Are you a senior brand partnerships and licensing professional who closes deals, owns projects end-to-end, and has the network to make things happen from day one? If so, read on.


YOUR TASKS

  • Partner Identification & Pipeline Management: You proactively source, evaluate, and pitch licensing and co-branding opportunities across entertainment IPs, cultural icons, celebrities, and lifestyle brands. You run an active pipeline of 5-10 live opportunities at any given time and know which ones are worth pursuing for our brand and commercial goals.

  • Deal Negotiation & Contracting: You lead negotiations end-to-end and close with confidence. LOIs, licensing agreements, talent contracts, commercial terms, royalties, usage rights. You represent us in front of top-tier partners, agents, and IP holders and you get deals across the line.

  • End-to-End Project Management: You own the full lifecycle of every limited edition. Concept, LOI, product development, packaging redesign, legal sign-off, market launch. You keep cross-functional teams across brand, product, design, legal, sales, retail, and D2C moving in the same direction and on time.

  • Business Case & Performance Ownership: You build and own the business case for every collaboration: budget, margin, revenue forecast, and post-launch review. You track revenue contribution, retail sell-through, D2C performance, and brand awareness lift per edition, and use it to make the next one better.

  • Internal Alignment & Launch Enablement: You brief and align brand, social, ecom, and retail on launch strategy, content needs, and sell-in materials so every edition lands the way it should, in-store and online.


YOUR PROFILE

  • You bring 5+ years in licensing, brand partnerships, or co-branding, ideally within FMCG, consumer lifestyle, entertainment, or a licensing/talent agency. You have taken 3+ limited editions or co-branded drops from concept to launch and can point to the results. You are a strategic thinker with a hands-on mindset and a proven execution track record.

  • You have negotiated and signed LOIs, licensing agreements, and talent contracts with full commercial responsibility. You come with a network of IP holders, agencies, talent managers, and entertainment companies that opens doors from day one.

  • You are comfortable juggling multiple complex workstreams at once, aligning cross-functional teams without formal authority, and holding a timeline without micromanaging. You have owned 6-7 figure budgets and built business cases from zero.

  • You communicate with confidence in both German and English. Native-level German and full fluency in English are required.

  • You take responsibility for your projects and your numbers, make clear decisions even when the path is not, and thrive where speed and ownership matter.


WHAT MAKES YOUR PROFILE COMPLETE

  • Experience working directly with entertainment studios, IP holders, or major talent agencies.
  • Background in FMCG, food & beverage, or better-for-you consumer brands.
  • Existing relationships in the DACH retail landscape with sell-in experience for limited editions.
  • Track record managing both D2C and retail launches at the same time.
  • Degree in Marketing, Media & Communications Management, Business Administration, or similar, though your track record matters far more than the diploma.


AND WHY AHEAD?

Working at ahead is more than just a job - it’s your opportunity to develop as a professional and as a person, while shaping the future of snacking. Our mission is to make low sugar the new standard, and we pour that ambition into every product we create. You’ll become part of a team where international talent, startup drive, real impact, and true ownership come together.

  • Hypergrowth Environment: If you're looking for greenfield, creative freedom, and real impact, you're in the right place. We're a team that is scaling fast - with purpose
  • Great Workspace: A central office in the heart of Hamburg near the Alster, top equipment (MacBook), snacks, drinks, plenty of ahead products - and yes, a ping-pong table. We’re also pet-friendly, so you can always bring your furry friend along
  • Amazing Team: Young, international, ambitious - inspiring colleagues who collaborate, support each other, and genuinely enjoy working together
  • Career Growth: Develop through cross-functional projects, structured feedback cycles, and a steep learning curve in a dynamic, high growth environment. We offer a fair, attractive salary with role-dependent bonus opportunities
  • Great Benefits: Fuel yourself with ahead snacks, drinks, and merch - we’ve got you covered. On top: a €50 monthly allowance to spend as you like - Urban Sports Club, mobility options, or vouchers from your favorite brands (IKEA, Rewe, Rossmann and more)
  • Vacation Days: Enjoy 28 vacation days plus two extra days off on December 24 (Christmas Eve) and December 31 (New Year’s Eve)
  • Events & Offsites: Regular after-work hangouts and legendary annual team offsites you won’t forget
For this role, you can choose whether to work from our offices in Hamburg or Berlin, or fully remotely from anywhere in Germany. If this sounds like a good fit, we would love to get to know you!

Staff GRC Analyst
description:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role

We're looking for a Staff GRC Analyst to join our Information Security team at Pleo. In this role, you'll help and be part of our governance operating model as we scale compliance. If you're excited about building compliance automation and are passionate about fast-paced scale ups, then this is the opportunity for you!

 

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to

You’ll report to our VP of Fraud & Security and work closely with teams in Risk and Compliance, Procurement, Legal, Finance, and Engineers. Our team is highly collaborative and dedicated to ensure compliance and security of the business. You’ll also have the chance to partner with teams across the organization to ensure success.

 

What you’ll be doing

As a Staff GRC Analyst, you will:

  • Automate our legacy systems relating to governance, risk, and compliance frameworks, including ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, DORA, UK Cyber Essentials and relevant financial services regulations.

  • Engineer GRC workflows with internal systems (e.g., ticketing, asset management, identity, cloud platforms) to support compliance by design.

  • Design and build scalable GRC architectures and automation for evidence collection, control testing, and compliance reporting.

  • Draft, review, and maintain Pleo's security policies, mapping them to relevant control standards and ensuring alignment across frameworks as the business evolves.

  • Automate incoming security requests from customers and prospects, including questionnaires, one-off questions, review calls, and documentation ensuring responses are accurate, thorough, and reflect our actual security posture.

  • Automate third-party vendor assessments, evaluating suppliers against Pleo's compliance and security standards and ensuring identified gaps are tracked and resolved.

  • Automate tracking and report on compliance metrics and KPIs, giving leadership the data-driven visibility they need to understand where the programme stands and where it needs to go.

  • Translate compliance requirements into technical specifications that engineering teams can implement, and make the same topics accessible to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Coordinate complex, multi-team workstreams, keeping dependencies visible, priorities clear, and delivery on track even when things shift.

  • Contribute to the broader Cybersecurity team, staying connected with ongoing initiatives and supporting shared goals across the function.

 

What you bring


You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

  • Significant experience in Security GRC, understanding of auditing processes, with direct experience in both internal and external audit cycles.

  • Demonstrated experience using AI and/or coding automation to get controls built, implemented, and operating in practice.

  • A strong understanding of cloud architectures (AWS or equivalent) and how infrastructure decisions map to security controls and audit evidence.

  • Experience automating reporting for GRC programs, including dashboards and executive-level summaries.

  • Fintech, payments industry or IT audit background, with familiarity with regulatory expectations and payment platform architectures.

  • Certifications such as CISM, CISSP, CISA, or PCI-related credentials. A degree in Cybersecurity, Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, or equivalent experience is a plus.

Why is this role a good fit for you

This role is a good fit for you if:

  • You're equally excited about getting into the details of regulations requirements as you are about writing code.

  • You demonstrate high-agency and like to take initiative in developing solutions that will save the team time.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

  • You are not able to work closely with colleagues who do not have an engineering background.

  • You require a well groomed backlog and task assignment in order to perform at your best.

How you’ll develop in this role

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll:

  • Get hands-on with Pleo's security landscape, learning how our GRC programme operates across frameworks like ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, and DORA.

  • Build automation for evidence collection, control testing, and policy as code within our existing compliance frameworks, and help shape the long-term security initiatives that support Pleo's growth, working closely with Engineering, Risk & Compliance, and other key stakeholders.

  • Integrate into the Cybersecurity team, connecting with ongoing initiatives, understanding shared goals, and starting to contribute to the workflows and tooling that keep Pleo secure and compliant.

We’re committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger projects, stepping into leadership, or acquiring new skills.

 

The location

Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.

 

Show me the benefits!

  • Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

  • Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

  • Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

  • We offer 25-28 days of holiday (depending on your location) + public holidays

  • For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

  • Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice

  • We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

  • Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

 

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we hired a GRC Analyst, we received a total of 350 applications but only 18 were selected for an intro call. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:

  • CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

About your application

  • English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

  • A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

  • Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

  • Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you.

  • Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

  • Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

  • Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

🌍 Represent n8n at events and in-market—building credibility with technical communities and enterprise leaders across Northern Europe (with customer travel as needed)

REQUIREMENTS

Must-haves

🏆 Enterprise SaaS sales track record: 5+ years in quota-carrying roles with consistent overachievement in enterprise segments

🧠 Consultative selling: You lead with customer outcomes, ask sharp questions, and tailor your narrative to the customer’s reality—not a generic pitch

Nice-to-haves

🧑‍💻 Open-source / community experience: You’ve sold in or alongside open-source ecosystems and understand bottoms-up adoption and PLG signals

🧪 Selling technical workflow/automation products: Experience with integration, API-first platforms, DevOps/SecOps/IT Ops, or adjacent categories

🚀 Early-stage / scale-up experience: You’ve helped build pipeline and playbooks in a fast-growing environment where process is evolving

description:

Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everybody involved in buying, selling, renting and letting property, regardless of their involvement, to improve the industry for everyone by elevating UK estate agencies through world-class technology.


Your job is to own the numbers for the entire commercial engine. Not hit them, own them. You'll build the single version of the truth that runs our marketing, sales and customer success functions, and put a reliable set of numbers in front of our leadership team and board.


You will take accountability for the integrity of the full commercial funnel from top-of-funnel marketing through to churn and renewals. Right now, each function applies its own definitions and rules. You'll set one consistent set of rules and make them stick across the entire business. You'll also be responsible for forecasting, headcount planning and supporting the design of commission structures.


This is a hands-on, senior operator role. You'll own the tech stack (HubSpot sits at the centre), and you'll build the workflows, automations and permissions that keep data clean at source. You're not tidying records by hand; you're designing systems. You'll also be working with AI daily – it's not optional here. We use Claude, and you'll need to show evidence of AI already embedded in how you work.


There are no commissions or bonuses in this role and that is deliberate. The role has to stay objective about what the figures say. We've positioned the salary to reflect both your seniority and the independence you'll need to challenge senior leaders professionally and diplomatically when the numbers don't match the narrative.

HERE'S WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT TO BE WORKING ON


  • Building and maintaining complete visibility across the entire revenue line: marketing pipeline, sales pipeline, churn and renewals, and capacity planning.

  • Setting and enforcing a single set of definitions and rules across marketing, sales and customer success, then making them stick.

  • Owning HubSpot end-to-end: permissions, day-to-day usage, workflow build, automations and the processes that keep data clean at source.

  • Producing forecasts, headcount plans and reporting that the leadership team can actually rely on.

  • Contributing to the design of commission plans and commercial structures.

  • Supporting the hiring and onboarding of a Sales Operations person, and training them to maintain what you've built.

  • Presenting to the board, with numbers that are clean, consistent and defensible.

  • Using AI to solve problems that would otherwise drown you in manual work.

  • Joining up the revenue line with the wider business (think product, finance, and marketing) so everybody's working from the same playbook.

WHY YOU SHOULD (AND SHOULDN'T) APPLY

YOU SHOULD APPLY IF:

  • You've owned reporting across a full commercial funnel (not just the sales pipeline). You can point to a forecast you owned, a commission plan you shaped and workflows you built yourself.

  • HubSpot is second nature to you. You operate at expert or power-user level and you can configure permissions, automations and processes without breaking into a sweat.

  • You've worked in multi-product SaaS at a senior level and you understand how different product lines affect pipeline, ARR and churn.

  • AI is already woven into how you work. You can give concrete examples of which tools you use, what you've built with them, and how they've changed your process significantly.

  • You can challenge senior leaders diplomatically but firmly, and you're not afraid to report the numbers as they actually are, not as people hope they'll be.

  • You work best with autonomy. You're a self-starter who gets the work done yourself, not someone who needs to manage others to feel productive.

  • You'd rather build something new than inherit a legacy system, and you're excited by the chance to define how commercial operations should work.


YOU PROBABLY SHOULDN'T APPLY IF:

  • You've spent your career managing the sales pipeline in isolation, without visibility into marketing and customer success.

  • You'd struggle with HubSpot or you'd need somebody else to handle the tech stack. This is not negotiable, unfortunately.

  • You need variable pay to feel motivated. Commission and bonus structures feel essential to you.

  • AI feels like a threat rather than a tool. You see it as something that reduces your value, not something that multiplies what you can deliver.

  • You need a large team beneath you from day one. This role starts solo and hands-on, though you'll build a team over time.

  • You'd rather build strategy than do the work. The first six months are about delivery—designing the systems, building the reports, making it stick—not sitting in planning meetings.


A BIT ABOUT YOU

Experience

You've spent time in a revenue operations, commercial operations or similar role, with demonstrable ownership of the full commercial funnel. You've done the work yourself – like configuring HubSpot, building forecasts, and leading alignment conversations across functions. Multi-product SaaS experience is non-negotiable; B2B exposure is strongly preferred.

 

Tooling

HubSpot sits at the centre, and you're an expert here. Experience with other platforms, such as Salesforce or Pipedrive, is a plus (some skills transfer). You're comfortable across other tech stacks and you use AI regularly as part of your workflow. Other tools in the stack will change and you're flexible on that front.


Communication

You can present to senior audiences without losing clarity. You push back on senior leaders when the numbers don't match the narrative, and you do it diplomatically enough that they listen rather than push back harder. You explain complex commercial logic in plain language.


Research

You think operationally. You diagnose what's broken in a process, you ask tough questions about data quality, and you can identify which problems to tackle first based on commercial impact. You're curious about how the business actually works, not just the metrics.

title: Associate Relationship Manager - London
description:
About Allica Bank

Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.

Department Description

Our vision is to reimagine Relationship Banking for established SMEs, through the very best people, products and digital tools. Allica’s Relationship Management team was formed in 2022 and continues to grow at pace, providing established SME customers with expert human relationships alongside modern banking technology.

The team supports customers with lending, current accounts, savings, asset finance and working capital facilities, while building deep local relationships with SME customers, trusted professional advisers and business communities.

The Associate Relationship Manager role is a newly created position that is a key step in our ambition to build the best Relationship team to support our SME clients. The successful candidate will manage a portfolio of clients and be expected to deliver across a range of commercial, customer service and risk objectives whilst also providing support to the wider relationship team as part of their development.

This is a great opportunity for someone looking to develop their skills and progress a career as an SME Relationship Manager.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Manage a portfolio of SME customers delivering outstanding customer service, building genuine and trusting relationships and develop a deep understanding of your clients’ businesses and their ambitions.

  • Deliver against a range of commercial targets including lending and new customer / deposit acquisition, as well as identifying and meeting a range of client needs through the provision of Allica products and services.

  • Build a trusted external network with SME advisers and the wider business community. Leverage this network to generate new business opportunities for the bank, in addition to signposting your clients to external support and advice as appropriate.

  • Ensure that Risk is managed effectively on your portfolio, with all required risk activities completed on time and to a high standard. Use customer data and internal Allica systems to identify signs of client stress and take proactive action to tackle early.

  • Work closely with a Senior Relationship Manager, contributing to building a bespoke personal development plan which will include supporting them and the wider team as part of your learning.

  • Take an active role in new business campaigns, including attending events, following up on leads, supporting prospect engagement and undertaking some cold calling where appropriate.

  • Support event organisation and follow-up activity, helping the team build strong local relationships with SME customers, prospects, accountants, solicitors and other trusted professional advisers.

  • Maintain accurate CRM records, strong follow-up discipline and good control over customer, prospect and portfolio activity.

  • Build strong, collaborative and productive relationships with your team and wider internal stakeholders to ensure customer needs are meet efficiently and any issues resolved quickly.

Personal Attributes & Experience

  • Some B2B sales, account management and/or SME banking experience, with a clear interest in building a career in SME relationship banking and a passion for supporting SMEs to be more successful.

  • Some experience of commercial lending and understanding / analysing financial accounts would be of benefit.

  • Curious, proactive and keen to learn, with the motivation to develop lending, sales, risk management and portfolio management capability through formal training and on-the-job coaching.

  • Confident engaging with customers, prospects and SME business advisers (including in person, via video call and by phone) asking great questions, following up consistently and building professional relationships.

  • Good organisation and attention to detail, with the ability to manage customer information and requests, portfolio tasks and follow-up actions accurately and at pace.

  • Practical understanding of customer service, sales activity and account management disciplines, ideally gained in a B2B, financial services or relationship-led environment.

  • Confident using systems, CRM tools and data to manage activity, track progress and support strong customer and risk outcomes.

  • Experience using AI tools in a business environment would also be of benefit.

  • An energetic, resilient, hands-on approach, with the confidence to get into the detail, solve problems and take ownership of outcomes.

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to build credibility with customers, prospects, advisers, colleagues and stakeholders.

  • Strong alignment to Allica’s values, with the judgement, integrity and energy to lead by example and help contribute to the next phase of the Direct Relationship Management channel.

Working at Allica Bank

At Allica Bank we want to ensure our employees have the right tools and environment in which to succeed in their role and in support of our customers.

Our employees are at the heart of everything we do, so our benefits are designed with you in mind:

  • Full onboarding support and continued development opportunities

  • Options for flexible working

  • Regular social activities

  • Pension contributions

  • Discretionary bonus scheme

  • Private health cover

  • Life assurance

  • Family friendly policies including enhanced Maternity & Paternity leave

Don’t tick every box?

Don’t worry if you don’t have all the skills or requirements listed on the job description. If you think you’ll be a good fit, we’d still love to hear from you!

Flexible working

We know the ‘9-to-5’ isn’t right for everyone. That’s why Allica Bank is fully committed to flexible and hybrid working. Please let us know what is best for you and, if we can, we will do our best to accommodate.

Diversity

We’re a diverse bunch here at Allica, with all kinds of experiences, backgrounds and lifestyles. Our openness and differences make us stronger, and we want everybody to feel comfortable bringing as much of themselves to work with them as they like.

The Product Owner will lead the work to define, deliver and manage AI-enabled products across our lending journeys, bringing together product design and thinking with a strong working knowledge of what today’s AI can and cannot do.

We're hiring the first dedicated owner of Omnea's performance marketing.

You're not starting from scratch. Paid campaigns, the website and our social channels all exist (and are working to varying degrees). But nobody's job is to work out what actually produces pipeline and then make more of it. That's this role: take what's already running, find the ROI, and professionalise it into something we can be proud of.

In one week you might work out why a paid campaign is generating leads that never convert, rebuild the landing page that's losing them, build a new LinkedIn audience off the back of our closed-won data, and show the exec team what the pipeline picture looks like.

If you want to run one channel and hand-off the numbers, this might not be for you. If you want to own the loop from spend through to pipeline, and have the data to prove what worked, it is.

Pipeline and performance

You'll build the picture of what marketing is actually returning, and you'll be the person with the answer when someone asks whether a channel is worth the money.

  • Own the pipeline number for our digital channels: how much, from where, and at what cost

  • Build and maintain dashboards in Dreamdata using sources like HubSpot and GA4

  • Track campaigns from first touch through to closed won, and use what you find to change what we run next

  • Run a proper testing cadence. Set the test, call the result, and stop the things that aren't working

  • Report on what the numbers mean, not only what they are

Paid

You own paid. Our agency handles campaign build and optimisation, and you set the direction they work to.

  • Own LinkedIn as our primary paid channel: audiences, target account lists, retargeting and sequencing

  • Build audiences from our own data: closed-won patterns, target accounts, product signals - rather than off-the-shelf targeting

  • Work with content and design teammates to produce compelling content

  • Make the case for more budget when the numbers justify it

Website and conversion

  • Own conversion across the site: forms, journeys, page structure, and what happens after someone clicks an ad

  • Build and update pages using our existing component library and CMS

  • Run an ongoing testing programme on the pages that matter, and work with the in-house design team on what comes next

  • Ship landing pages for campaigns and product launches, including forms and tracking

  • Keep tracking and attribution clean, so the reporting can be trusted

What we're looking for

  • Experience in a B2B marketing role, in-house or agency. We care more about what you delivered than where you did it.

  • You're commercial. You think in pipeline and cost per opportunity, not clicks and impressions, and you can tell the difference between a campaign that's busy and one that's working.

  • You know paid mechanics properly. Audiences, match rates, attribution windows, frequency. LinkedIn Ads specifically.

  • You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a report from scratch, spot when something looks wrong, and explain a trend to someone who wasn't in the weeds with you.

  • You've built pages in a CMS. Not from scratch in code — assembling pages from components, keeping them consistent, and getting the tracking right.

  • Comfortable in tools like HubSpot, Dreamdata, Google Ads, Campaign Manager

  • B2B SaaS, ideally selling to finance, procurement, legal or risk

  • SEO fundamentals

title: S&O Manager - Rider Fraud
description:
About the role

This role will lead our approach to understanding and reducing courier/rider fraud and abuse across Wolt and Deliveroo. Combining data-led investigation with strong operational judgement, you will identify emerging risk patterns, understand the features of our operating models that may contribute to those risks, and assess their potential impact.

A key part of the role is turning insight into action. You will translate analysis into clear, proportionate policies and operational responses that protect platform integrity and customer outcomes, while remaining practical to implement and appropriate for the markets in which we operate. You will work closely with Legal, Public Policy, Product, Data Science and Operations to navigate complex legal and regulatory considerations and ensure our approach is effective, fair and robust.

Core responsibilities

  • Lead a programme of work to identify, assess and prioritise courier/rider fraud and abuse risks across Wolt and Deliveroo.

  • Translate identified risks into proportionate policy, process and operational responses, balancing risk reduction with customer outcomes, courier/rider experience and business practicality.

  • Lead the implementation, monitoring and ongoing refinement of fraud and abuse policies, with clear measures of effectiveness and residual risk.

  • Ensure policy approaches are developed with appropriate consideration of legal, regulatory, compliance and reputational implications.

What you’ll be doing

  • Build a deep understanding of our courier/rider operating models, incentive structures and end-to-end journeys to identify where fraud or abuse risk may arise, using data, operational knowledge and structured, hypothesis-led analysis.

  • Develop analytical approaches and key metrics to identify patterns, quantify impact, assess detection signals and measure the effectiveness of policy interventions over time.

  • Define new policies, or revise existing ones, in response to identified risks that may negatively affect customers, couriers/riders, the platform or the wider business.

  • Conduct impact and risk assessments, framing clear options and recommendations that consider effectiveness, operational feasibility, cost, legal and regulatory requirements, and potential unintended consequences.

  • Partner closely with Legal, Public Policy, Product, Data Science, Trust and Operations teams to shape business requirements, implement agreed responses and resolve complex trade-offs.

  • Establish effective ways of working across Wolt and Deliveroo so that emerging trends, priority risks and lessons from policy performance are identified early and shared with relevant stakeholders.

  • Lead cross-functional delivery from problem identification through to implementation, reporting and post-launch monitoring, adapting the approach as new evidence emerges.


What we’re looking for

  • 6+ years’ experience in fraud, risk, compliance, policy, operations, consulting or a related field.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to combine data, operational context and judgement to identify root causes and prioritise action.

  • Experience translating complex or ambiguous risk issues into practical policies, recommendations and implementation plans.

  • Experience navigating complex legal and regulatory landscapes and working constructively with Legal and Public Policy stakeholders.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to influence senior and cross-functional stakeholders and challenge constructively when needed.

  • Comfortable using AI-enabled tools appropriately to support analysis, hypothesis generation and problem solving.

 

Why Deliveroo

title: Senior Customer Support Engineer
description:
About Fyxer

Since launching in May 2024 we've grown to $30 million in ARR. Fyxer is building an AI executive assistant that handles emails, scheduling and follow-up, freeing people in client-facing roles to focus on their customers.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own the hardest technical tickets in the business end to end, including the customer conversation, from first report through to resolution

  • Dogfood Fyxer’s own products, give feedback, and influence our roadmap

  • Establish blast radius before escalating, because one customer reporting something is a ticket and forty-seven accounts in the same broken state is an incident

  • Call bug, incident or user error correctly and quickly, and declare it when it's an incident

  • Write escalations Engineering can act on without a single follow-up question, and stay on them until they land

  • Spot patterns across Linear and the queue, raising a tracker before the fifth report of something becomes the tenth

  • Reduce the need for your own role through runbooks, saved queries, Parahelp knowledge, and hands-on upskilling of our senior agents

Here's the honest version of why this role exists. In one recent three-month window we escalated 47 tickets to Engineering and two of them were resolved. Engineering is capacity-constrained, and a third of what we sent them was correctly deprioritised. So this isn't a role that escalates better, it's one that resolves. You'll be backed by strong Customer Success and Product Engineering teams, and given read-only access to our codebase through Cursor, to our data through our internal tooling, and to our production logs to do it.

What Success Looks Like

  • You resolve a growing share of technical escalations without Engineering ever being involved

  • Your escalations are complete, so Engineer can act on them quickly

  • You use AI and you catch it when it's wrong, before it reaches a customer

  • You hold a customer's confidence while you investigate, rather than handing them back to someone else

  • Our senior agents are visibly more capable six months in than they are today, because of you

  • You're the person the team wants on the ticket because they trust your judgement.

What You Bring

  • 3+ years in a technical support role within a SaaS or cloud-based company

  • API fluency: you can read an API reference, reason about authentication, and say what a 401 rather than a 500 tells you about where the fault sits

  • SQL you write yourself: given an unfamiliar schema you work out how the tables relate and write the join unaided

  • Comfortable in logs, following a request across services and working backwards from an error

  • Strong written communication, particularly to a customer who is unhappy

  • Experience with customer support tools such as Zendesk, Intercom, Jira, Linear, others

  • Startup-ready: adaptable, fast-moving, and hands-on

We're not asking for production engineering experience or a computer science degree. We care what you can do, not how you got there.

Location and other bits

  • Based in our Chancery Lane office in London, Monday to Thursday, with Fridays from home

  • Standard office hours

  • Benefits include: on-site gym, private medical, pension and lunch provided everyday

The Hiring Process

  1. Submit your CV (no need for a cover letter)

  2. We'll review it

  3. An initial call with someone from the hiring team to review your experience and motivation for joining (30 mins)

  4. A call with our Head of Customer Support on your experience and how you think technically (30 minutes)

  5. A live technical exercise (60 minutes)

  6. Meet more of the team (30 minutes)

For the exercise we'll give you access to a small example application, a database, an API and its logs, a couple of days ahead, along with three customer tickets. You don't need to solve anything in advance, and you're welcome to use whatever AI tooling you normally would, because that's how the job actually works. title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

We’re already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $500m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

Why we’re hiring

  • We're post-PMF and revenue generating, launching in the US ahead of a Series A. Early enough that you'll shape how engineering works here, late enough that you're not gambling on whether the product works.

  • You'll own significant parts of the product and ship the things customers feel most. It's a regulated platform moving money across multiple jurisdictions, so the work has to be right and it still has to be fast.

  • We also want the bar to move while you're here. Senior engineers set the standard through the quality of what they ship, how they review, and the problems they choose to fix rather than work around.

  • Alongside that, we're rethinking how we build with AI. We use the tools, but we know there's a step change available to teams who redesign their whole workflow around them rather than adding AI to how they already work. If you've already done that somewhere else, you'll have a lot of room here.

What we're looking for

  • You've built and run non-trivial production systems, and you've learned what works in which situations rather than defaulting to one approach.

  • Strong architectural judgement. Most of our code is now written by an LLM, which means you need to own the decisions around it: how the system is structured, what the patterns are, whether the thing being built is the right thing at all. Our stack is Go, and if you learn quickly, not having written it isn't a problem.

  • A serious AI practice. You can talk specifically about how AI has changed the way you build, what it's actually made faster, and what you've shared with the teams you've worked in.

  • Directness. You give feedback when something isn't good enough and take it just as well.

  • Good instincts about what's worth doing. You know when something needs to be built properly and when it doesn't, and you push for the work that makes everyone around you faster.

Probably not for you if

You think the impact of AI on engineering is overstated. You'd rather be handed a fully specified ticket than question the brief. Or the learning curve across finance, compliance and multiple jurisdictions sounds like a chore rather than the interesting part.

The people who do well here find that last bit genuinely interesting. Understanding how capital actually moves, and what the rules allow in each jurisdiction, is most of what makes this product hard to build and hard to copy.

Three stages, usually inside two weeks, with detailed feedback within 24 hours of each one.

  1. Call with Imani, our Head of People and Talent. You'll get a proper picture of the role and the company, and we'll get into how you work and how you build.

  3. Paid trial day. A real Odin problem with everything you need handed to you. You see how we work, we see how you ship.

Working at Odin

Two setups work for this role: London hybrid (three days a week in the office) or remote from elsewhere in Europe with quarterly trips to London.

description:

Private markets are overdue a design transformation, and there is still no design-led company setting the standard for the category. Most products in the space look and feel like a bank statement from 2009. We’re looking for someone to help us change that.

Odin is building infrastructure for the future of private markets. We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should be putting it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.
